Best quality prefers TrueHD and Atmos, then DTS-HD, lossless, DTS, Dolby Digital Plus, then the most channels. Commentary tracks are skipped.

During playback press Info, Menu or Guide to choose a subtitle (★ = made for this exact file) and to move its timing earlier or later.

Everything on this TV is replaced with the backup, then Ember restarts.
FFmpeg decodes audio the TV cannot: TrueHD, DTS, DTS-HD core, Dolby Digital (Plus), FLAC, ALAC.
\"Fill in\" keeps what your addon gives and adds what is missing. \"Replace\" prefers AniList and TVDB. Anime are titles with an anime type or id, or an Anime or Animation genre.
For a new TV or after reinstalling.
For a receiver or soundbar over HDMI.

For receivers, soundbars and projectors that delay the sound or the picture. Fine-tune while watching in the Info panel.
For services that need one. Keys entered here are stored encrypted on this TV and replace the ones built into the app.
For the built-in player. Found when a video starts, ranked, and picked for you.
Frame-rate matching plays 23.976 fps films at 23.976 Hz (no judder). The screen may go dark for a moment when it switches.
Free, no key. Found by title and year.
Hold OK on a source to choose a player; on your media server sources it also offers playback quality and server actions.
Hold OK on an app to move it, remove it from Home, or hide it from this page.

How long Home waits for an addon\'s catalog before skipping it. Sources get twice as long, and appear as each addon answers.

If Ember closes by itself, the details are kept here on the TV (nothing is sent). Copy or photograph one when reporting a problem.

Keeps menus and the clock clear of the edges on projectors and TVs that crop the picture (overscan).
Large keeps up to two minutes or 200 MB ahead, enough for 80–100 Mbps remuxes. Huge allows 400 MB; use it only on devices with 3 GB of memory or more.
Lists the streaming services that have a title, on its title screen.
Logins and links are stored encrypted on this TV and are included in backups. Use a connected keyboard to enter long links more easily.
Makes everything on screen smaller or larger: cards, rows, menus and text.
Match the display to the video, like a disc player.
\"Match to the exact file\" reads 128 KB from the start and end of the video to compute its OpenSubtitles hash; subtitles with the same hash were timed on that very file.
Night: dark. Day: light backgrounds and dark text. Auto: day from 7 am to 7 pm, night otherwise.

Put the backup somewhere the TV can download it, such as Dropbox (change the end of the link to ?dl=1) or a secret GitHub gist (use its Raw link). Use a passphrase if the file is online.
Recommended, Because you watched, Hidden gems and your lists.

Shown on title screens, under the title, in this order.

Standard: the full Settings page. Floating: a quick panel over the screen you are on, with your most-used settings and shortcuts to the full pages; the remote\'s Menu key also opens it.
Switch off what you don\'t use. Off features load nothing when Ember starts, so Home opens faster.
Switch sections on or off and move them. Catalog rows come from Settings > Catalogs. Extra rows need Trakt; Hidden gems needs a TMDB key.
Switched off in Settings > Features, so nothing is loaded and the tab is hidden.
Templates use the same syntax as AIOStreams\' custom formatter, so you can paste one made there.
Text only, on top of the interface size. Larger helps from across the room.
The large picture at the top of Home.
The order is shared: Home rows and the Discover list both follow it. Catalogs that need a search term or a genre can be used in Discover but not as Home rows.
Only this session\'s code works. Phone setup turns off after 15 minutes or when you leave this screen. Switch it off when you finish.
The video\'s own subtitle in your language is used first (perfect timing); otherwise the best-ranked download. Forced subtitles in the video still show.
This is a debug build. Updates are signed release builds, which install over it only after you uninstall this one (set up the signing key, see BUILDING.md).
Phone setup could not start. Check the TV Wi-Fi or Ethernet connection and try turning it on again.
Title art slowly changes between your titles\' backdrops. Black suits OLED screens.
Trakt, Simkl and the rest: Continue watching, watchlists and reporting what you watch.
True black backgrounds at night: deeper blacks on OLED TVs and less glow from a projector.
TVDB is found by the title\'s IMDb id. With \"Also for anime\", AniList\'s description and artwork still win for anime when both are on.
Type at least two letters, or press Voice. The search key on your remote also starts voice search here.
Use a connected keyboard to enter long keys more easily. Keys are included in backups, so you only enter them once.
Used when you pick a source. Hold OK on a source to choose a player for one play.

Uses intro, recap and credits markers from your server, with optional IntroDB fallback when none are available. Community timings may vary by release. In the credits the button goes to the next episode.
Very large files need a fast connection.

Video uses the TV\'s hardware decoders (HEVC, AV1, VP9, H.264, Dolby Vision where supported; Dolby Vision falls back to HDR10 when it is not). If the TV\'s decoder fails, FFmpeg decodes the video in software (H.264, HEVC including 10-bit, VP8, VP9): fine up to 1080p, slow for 4K on most TVs. Choose Always FFmpeg on emulators and virtual machines, whose video decoders are often missing or limited.
TV, then FFmpeg if it fails

Your services. Ones with an installed app start on.
Wide cards in rows and Watch next. Movie and show artwork is a photo from the film; this adds the title the way posters have it.
The title\'s logo over its backdrop. Logos come from your addon, else from Metahub (free, needs an IMDb id). Titles without a logo show their name.
RPDB\'s backdrops with rating badges, plus the title\'s logo. Titles RPDB does not have keep their own backdrop.
RPDB backdrops need a Tier 2 key or higher (Settings > API keys). Until then the photo with title logo is used.
The backdrop with the name written on it, as before.
The small tags under each source (4K, DV, Atmos, 7.1…).
Choose which Detailed badge categories to show. Highlighted categories are on. Your choices are saved; Basic and Custom packs are unaffected.

Colour badges for quality, resolution, visuals, audio, channels, video codecs, languages and streaming services. Visual, audio and channel badges use transparent tier-style chips with grey outlines; languages use the resolution badges\' amber style. All images are built into Ember for offline use. Badges appear when the source provides the matching information.
Ember\'s own text tags: HDR, codec, sound, languages, size. The default.
Your own pack: a badge JSON file (\"filters\" with a pattern and an image or colours). Enter its link, or send the file from Settings > Phone setup.

Ember: the remote\'s Settings or Menu button opens Ember\'s settings (and the info panel while playing). TV: Ember leaves these buttons alone, for TVs and projectors that use them for their own menus (picture mode, focus, keystone).

Basic: standard playback controls. Ember Modern: glass buttons, title details and episode controls. Ember X: cinema-style controls. Streaming: buttons top left, title top right, the title logo on the left and sound and subtitle choices under the progress bar. Independent of your launcher interface; applies the next time you open a movie or episode. Live TV and trailers keep their dedicated controls.
